Definition: Is the register integrated with the government's national data exchange system?
Comments: Integration with govt systems for interoperability starting with Finance ministry.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed. Corroborated with the original French-language report: on 10 March 2026 Chad's Ministry of Finance and ANATS signed a protocol to allow secure consultation of the biometric population register for identity verification in financial/administrative procedures. This is a newly signed agreement enabling future real-time data sharing, not yet an operational connection across government — 'Under development' (3) remains the best fit; 'Partially integrated' (4) would overstate a just-signed protocol.

Definition: Is the register integrated with the national ID system?
Comments: It is the national ID/biometric system.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed. World Bank's Chad Digital Transformation Project appraisal document confirms the population register and national ID system are the same platform (SIGPTS, managed by ANATS), with the National Biometric Register of Populations (RNBP) module issuing the unique National Identification Number (NIN/NNI) used for the ID card, passport and other credentials. Integration is definitional, so 'Fully integrated nationwide' (5) is supported.

Definition: Are all non-citizens allowed to be included in the register?
Comments: Includes citizens and refugees (pilot issuing biometric IDs and NNIRs to thousands of refugees).
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Revised down. The cited source describes a pilot only (started in N'Djamena, ~4,000 IDs issued by May 2025 against a phased target of 25,000), restricted to refugees aged 10+, against a refugee population of over 1.24 million (World Bank, Nov 2024) — not the whole non-citizen population and not yet national in scope. This supports 'Some refugees and IDPs' (3) rather than 'All included' (4); no evidence found of eligibility for other non-citizen categories (e.g. all IDPs, stateless persons, asylum seekers generally).

Definition: What proportion of the population does the register cover?
Comments: Database of 15M records in country of ~21M pop (~70% coverage) but exact recent uptake unknown; rated conservative as partial/full.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Revised down substantially. The original 15 million figure is the system's biometric de-duplication capacity at 2020 launch, not enrolled population, as the cited source itself states ('capability to deduplicate ... against a database of 15 million people'). The authoritative World Bank Chad Digital Transformation Project appraisal document states that only 3% of the Chadian population aged over 12 possess a National ID card, with a significant gender gap. This places actual coverage in the '<20%' band (1), not '50-69%' (3).

Definition: Does the government maintain one or more social protection registers?
Comments: Unified Social Registry under strengthening per World Bank Sahel project.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Revised up. The Unified Social Registry (Registre Social Unifié, RSU) was established in 2016 and transferred to INSEED in 2019 (Government Decree). World Bank's June 2024 Project Appraisal Document records the RSU already covering roughly 600,000 households across 15 provinces (including refugees), and INSEED's own site documents active household-enrolment campaigns extending the RSU as recently as January 2026. This is an operating, expanding system rather than one merely 'under development' — 'Partially deployed' (4) better reflects the evidence; full nationwide deployment is not yet demonstrated.
